title: The man who knows himself has no enemies (Jung Lecture + Dream Analysis)
summary: First Wednesday philosophy stream: NH lectures on the first half of chapter 3 (The Aims of Psychotherapy) of Jung's Modern Man in Search of a Soul, covering the morning/afternoon/twilight of life, psychic context, loss of meaning as the general neurosis of our time, and the role of dreams. He then interprets viewers' dreams live using Jungian archetypes, with tangents on autism, single mothers, taurine for sleep and Dracula.
claims: Knowing yourself removes enemies: once you understand that problems are manifestations of your own unconscious, they become things within your control

The conjugate system is decent for hypertrophy and Louis Simmons was one of the best non-bodybuilding coaches; Westside lifters had great triceps, so bodybuilders should copy good methods even from non-bodybuilders
He has read Beyond Good and Evil more than 10 times and still rediscovers themes when discussing it with a philosophy client
He uses Ko-fi instead of Patreon because Ko-fi takes no cut and allows private message exchanges with supporters

Psychological theories reflect the society and person that produced them: Freud's sexual theory arose in a sexually repressive culture, and a German therapist would likely produce a different theory than an American one

People respond to the school of psychology that fits their needs; if therapy fails it may mean the approach does not suit the person, not that the method is worthless, so you are responsible for finding your own method
Jung is trustworthy because he admits his own views are relative and subjective, unlike many people on YouTube fitness who claim objectivity for themselves
Psychology is a baby science; we have explored perhaps 2% of the human psyche, and claims that it is mapped out are bogus

Failures teach far more than successes; a victory just confirms your game plan, while a loss gives you homework. This applies to the gym too, and seeing failure as an opportunity removes it as an enemy
He is best placed to advise young men in their late teens and early 20s because he has lived it, but can only guess about the 35-45 'afternoon' stage
The main neurosis of the young is fear of growth and responsibility (the puer aeternus / man-child); the main neurosis of the old is clinging to youth and shrinking back from death

A man should expand like a supernova in his prime and accept the later contraction; in old age strength and vitality should be replaced by wisdom, as in traditional tribes where young men hunted and old men were valued for wisdom
Watching an old man in a French bus melt down shouting he used to squat heavy weights when he could not step off unaided showed him the pain of clinging to lost strength
Plastic surgery to stay young is childish; people just look younger in lizard years

Men raised by single mothers often remain emotionally enmeshed (what Jung calls an incest relation); mothers instinctively constrict boys' risk-taking, and the father's role is to let the boy take risks and become a man
Instead of rushing to antidepressants, first get depressed inactive people to do physical activity
Men should seek therapy from men; men need shorter, actionable sessions, and self-improvement is essentially mass therapy for men built on action lists and discipline
To find who you are, spend time alone and stop numbing yourself with cheap pleasures, low media, binging and drugs
Society has normalized mental illness so people make neuroses part of their personality instead of facing their shadow; being poorly adapted is now framed as healthy
Spirituality is not religion: it means believing in the unseen (e.g. the unconscious) and valuing things that are not material; he considers himself spiritually inclined and extremely introverted
Most human actions are driven by instinct; reason is a young psychic technology and humans may become less emotional but also less human
Introversion is part nature, part nurture: his twin two-year-old nieces already show opposite temperaments
He is likely on the autism spectrum (undiagnosed) and is glad he was never treated as special; autistic people should be gradually exposed and taught coping skills, and everyone masks

As a child he walked on tiptoes, imagined Pokemon jumping across buildings, memorized animal names from documentaries and quizzed adults, once getting grounded for correcting an adult who called sharks mammals
About a third of Jung's patients suffered from senselessness and emptiness of life; loss of meaning is the general neurosis of our time, despite unprecedented material comfort
Feeling stuck despite having money, education and a job is a spiritual problem with no material solution
Myths across unconnected cultures tell the same hero story because humans share the same psychic context
Dreams must serve a purpose since evolution spends precious resources on them, like the thumb; they carry messages from the unconscious
A dream interpretation is valid if the dreamer finds meaning in it and it gets them unstuck; demanding scientific proof is autoerotic
He keeps dreaming of playing football, which he quit as a teen out of boredom; he reads it as a reminder to regain his ability to stick with commitments
Taking taurine before bed gave him very vivid dreams, deeper sleep and staying in REM without waking; it costs about 10 dollars for six months
Apparently prophetic dreams are the brain recognizing past patterns and warning you, not true prophecy
The brain encodes truths in symbols because the harsh truth stated outright might be too much to bear
People only accept suggestions they already secretly agree with; a wrong interpretation is simply rejected by the psyche
Men dream of fighting intruders and bears because of a protective instinct; he claims women do not have such dreams
Being ineffective at violence in dreams signals lack of confidence and a repressed animal side, common in modern men
A dream where you are chased by an animal means you must stop running and confront your problems; avoidance lets the problem in deeper
His recurring dream of failing school exams comes from his first year of college in France when he skipped class out of boredom and barely passed despite being capable of topping the class
To overcome social anxiety, develop a self you are not afraid to show; fear of judgment means there are things in you that you dislike
To become eloquent, speak in public as much as possible, e.g. a Toastmasters club
Verbal bullying is as damaging as physical; respond verbally to verbal aggression and dish it back
Heel-elevated squats are good for rectus femoris and he feels them more in the VMO than normal squats, but they may not develop all quad heads equally, so also include split squats
People remember nightmares more than pleasant dreams because focusing on the negative aids survival
Dracula reflects British colonial-era fear of the foreign invading the motherland and corrupting women's sexuality
Jujutsu Kaisen and Dune contain Jungian themes; Paul's prophecy in Dune is pattern recognition from the past
exercises: good for rectus femoris and VMO; pair with split squats
complement to heel-elevated squats for all quad heads
viewer_questions: should men seek therapy from men
how to find who you are
what if you don't remember dreams
